ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle with G as the center, J is on the circle, and the horizontal segment JH is tangent to the circle at point J. The vertical segment GJ is labeled x. A slanted line extends from G through point K on the circle to H, where GK is labeled x and KH is labeled 8, so GH = x + 8. The horizontal tangent segment JH is labeled 12. Reasoning: Because JH is the tangent to the circle at point J, radius GJ is perpendicular to tangent JH, so triangle GJH is a right triangle with J as the right angle. By the Pythagorean theorem, GJ^2 + JH^2 = GH^2, that is, x^2 + 12^2 = (x + 8)^2. Expanding gives x^2 + 144 = x^2 + 16x + 64, so 144 = 16x + 64, 80 = 16x, x = 5.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at G, with J on the circle and segment JH tangent at J. The vertical segment GJ is labeled x, so it is a radius. The slanted segment from G through K to H has GK labeled x, also a radius, and KH labeled 8, so GH = x + 8. The horizontal tangent segment JH is labeled 12. Use the tangent-radius theorem: a radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, so triangle GJH is right at J. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: GJ^2 + JH^2 = GH^2, giving x^2 + 12^2 = (x+8)^2. Solve to get x = 5.
